cases.prompt: Diagnose an interrupted write Run using only these retained facts. At 10:00 Central delivered Run R under Bridge epoch 5. At 10:01 the socket disconnected after the external service accepted a request but before a response was retained. At 10:02 Bridge restarted at epoch 6; Central still shows R working with cancellation pending. The local journal says external commit outcome UNKNOWN. The external service supports a read-only lookup by retained operation ID; repeating the request without checking can apply the write twice. A later epoch-5 completion callback arrives. Rules: Central owns canonical Run state and rejects stale-epoch callbacks; transport loss is not evidence that an external write did not commit. Deliver: distinguish transport, Run and external-effect states; the safe next diagnostic action and retry boundary; handling of the late callback; the truthful owner-facing status and an acceptance test for duplicate-effect prevention.

rubric.text: Distinguishes disconnection, still-working/cancellation-pending Run and unknown external commit; does not equate UNKNOWN with not committed.
Uses the retained operation ID for read-only reconciliation before any retry and avoids blindly repeating the write.
Rejects the stale epoch-5 callback as a current lifecycle transition while recognizing that this does not prove no external effect.
Shows pending/unknown status without success or zero-effect claims and proposes a test preventing duplicate writes across the disconnect/restart.

cases.prompt: Correct one Discussion status panel. createdAt=10:00:00, terminalAt=10:00:30, observedAt=10:02:00. Three member slots were debited. One Run completed; a second Run is still working under cancellation; the third member failed before any Run was created. The panel currently says "3 completed Runs, 120 seconds Discussion elapsed". Give created/completed/working Run counts, unbound/debited slot counts, the correct Discussion wall duration including waits, and what changes if the second Run later completes. The terminalAt timestamp remains 10:00:30. No other metrics are requested.

rubric.text: Reports two created Runs, one completed and one still working.
Reports one unbound slot and three debited budget slots.
Reports 30 seconds of Discussion wall time including waits.
Later completion changes completed to two and working to zero while wall duration remains 30 seconds.

cases.prompt: Compare deployment choices through transport security, operations and user experience. Supplied constraints: a trusted LAN installation has no public domain or Internet; browsers must work without installing a private CA; Bridge must keep a pinned private-CA HTTPS channel; existing data and Device credentials must survive transport changes. Plain LAN browser HTTP is allowed only with explicit owner acceptance of unencrypted browser traffic. A uses HTTP for both browser and Bridge. B uses owner-approved LAN browser HTTP and a separate pinned HTTPS Bridge endpoint. C requires public-CA HTTPS using a public domain and Internet. Choose the feasible option, explain why the other two fail, describe the owner-facing tradeoff without claiming encryption for browser HTTP, and propose validation for browser access, wrong-CA rejection and preserved data/Device credentials. Do not change any installation.

rubric.text: Chooses B with separate LAN browser HTTP and pinned Bridge HTTPS under explicit owner acceptance.
Rejects A for losing Bridge HTTPS pinning and C for unavailable public domain/Internet.
Clearly states browser traffic remains unencrypted and requires owner acceptance; does not claim end-to-end HTTPS.
Covers CA-free browser access, wrong-CA Bridge rejection and preservation of data and Device credentials.

cases.prompt: Compare two fixed schedules. Job A takes 8 seconds; independent Job B takes 13 seconds. A required finalizer starts only after both jobs finish and takes 4 seconds. There is no overhead, contention or failure. Option S runs A then B then finalizer. Option P starts A and B together then runs finalizer. Compute both wall times, choose the schedule meeting a 20-second deadline, and explain whether this timing comparison proves better answer quality. Use the supplied assumptions; no new agents or routing algorithm are needed.

rubric.text: Calculates sequential wall time as 25 seconds.
Calculates parallel wall time as 17 seconds, including the finalizer.
Chooses P as the only option meeting the 20-second deadline.
Does not infer better answer quality from wall time or invent additional overhead contrary to the premise.
